# Energy execution review | Wednesday 11 November 2026
**Selective adverse-selection evidence in utility oil flow; no desk-wide exchange execution failure.**
Session: 00:00-24:00 UTC, also London time on this date. Bookings frozen at 12 Nov 09:20 UTC. 2,757 exchange fills plus 252 original broker/OTC deals; two non-exchange cancellations leave 250 valid deals. No automatic refresh.

**Utility oil:** 32 fresh paired observations, five-minute mean **-5.58 bps**, weighted **-5.14 bps**, **-$81,235** hypothetical markout. Of that, **-$55,868** is movement after the fill (mean -4.08 bps, descriptive t=-3.54). A matched subset of 15 is -6.98 bps worse than exchange peers (t=-3.10). Review UTILITY_01 and UTILITY_05 first, but their samples are only five and three trades. Industrial flow is a weaker watch item.

**Do not confuse:** spread crossing in gasoil; the 09:30 gas/power repricing and model failure; a Brent inventory-limit exceedance; manual marks, volatility corrections, delayed bookings and the EEX feed gap. Panels below retain the SQL and trade IDs.

cells.value:
**Panels 01-08.** Negative markout is bad for the desk. It is a hypothetical mark-to-mid value, not realized P&L, and excludes fees and subsequent hedging. Arrival markout includes spread paid; subtract arrival from the five-minute markout to isolate subsequent price movement. Curves use fresh quotes independently at each horizon, so counts vary. Panels 04-07 require fresh quotes at both endpoints.
The utility effect is adverse on both sides and in Brent, WTI and gasoil. The previous day has the same direction (25 paired utility trades, -4.01 bps total, -2.37 bps after fill, t=-1.50), but is not independently conclusive. Peer matching covers only 15 of 32 trades, with 1-5 peers each; size/channel differences remain. Per-trade t statistics are descriptive, unadjusted for correlated trades or searching many segments. This supports targeted review, not proof of informed intent or a causal counterparty ranking. Clearing houses on exchange bookings are not the executing counterparties.
Industrial oil: 26 paired trades, -4.14 bps total, -2.98 bps after fill (t=-1.46); matched excess -1.73 bps (15 trades, t=-0.57). Treat as a hypothesis.

cells.value:
**Gasoil:** fresh exchange fills pay about 1.48 bps half-spread and only 0.034 bps beyond touch. Mean markout is -1.51 bps at arrival and -1.30 bps at five minutes. This is mainly spread cost, not evidence of persistent picking off.
**Gas/power:** January TTF and NBP rose about 7%, and UK power about 6%, from 09:29 to 09:50. For NBP fills during 09:00-10:00, 25 sells mark -283 bps at 30 minutes while nine buys mark +301 bps; other-hour sells average +4.97 bps. A common directional shock explains much of the apparent venue loss. No external event cause is established.
After 09:30 the champion winter model is biased about -432 bps in TTF, -430 in NBP and -360 in UK power, versus roughly -9 to -11 bps for the challenger. Input timestamps are current in the stored model rows. This is model mispricing, not evidence of stale input timestamps; there is no order-to-model linkage proving it caused fills.
**Brent:** reconstructed net inventory peaks at 2,931,000 bbl at 07:29:26, 146.55% of the recorded 2,000,000 bbl limit. It includes opening positions and corrected exchange/OTC bookings. The limit master is dated 12 Nov, so this is a comparison to the available limit, not proof of the exact limit then effective. Brent exchange five-minute markouts are positive overall.

## Method and limitations
All execution queries retain **11 November 2026** literally. The booking cutoff is **12 November 2026 09:20 UTC**. Version-one events identify original trade times; latest bookings before the cutoff supply corrected price, quantity and book, and cancellations are excluded. Exchange fills and exchange booking rows are not counted twice. Exchange benchmarks use the execution venue; broker/OTC benchmarks use the primary source (ICE, ICE_ENDEX or CME). HORIZON joins use the last quote at or before the target; quotes older than 30 seconds are excluded from scorecards. Panel 08 deliberately retains all utility oil trades with ages for audit. Five-minute exchange coverage is 2,664/2,757 (96.6%).
Signed markout = sign(qty) * (future mid - corrected fill price). Currency markout = (future mid - price) * signed quantity * instrument px_factor. NBP prices are pence, so px_factor=0.01. Volume remains in the displayed instrument units; currencies are not summed. Native P&L and notional-weighted bps accompany means. Panel 09 assesses original recorded execution prices.
The three-minute EEX gap is **08:45-08:48 UTC**, with no EEX fills during it. TTF Q1-27 had 30 manual version-one marks by trader_11 at **08:00-08:29**, about **EUR 2.50/MWh** above the month strip; version two corrects them by EUR 2.50. Four TTF March ATM volatility marks at **10:30-10:45** were revised upward by **8 volatility points**. These are market-data/valuation controls, not measured execution losses. No option positions are supplied for valuing the volatility effect.
**34 trades booked next day** (8 broker, 26 OTC); **13 amendments and two cancellations** affect this session. Booking-time analysis would misattribute these trades. Raw marks have effective timestamps and versions, but no separate publication time, so the exact time a correction became known cannot be reconstructed.

## Coverage
| Source | Check and result |
|---|---|
| energy_fills, energy_trade_events | Full session, venue/passivity/side/trader/size/time splits, markouts, lifecycle and delayed booking checks. |
| energy_quotes | Same-venue or primary quotes, pre/post horizons, freshness exclusions, front-contract feed gaps. 10s/1m/5m/1d rollups checked through lineage; 1m used for market context. |
| energy_instruments, energy_listings | 243 instruments, 352 listings, primary listing present for all 243, price/currency/unit factors checked. Current master snapshot only. |
| energy_curve_marks, energy_curve_marks_1h | Version/source checks and duration-weighted strip consistency. Manual TTF anomaly; hourly derivative lineage checked. |
| energy_model_prices, energy_model_graded_day | All two-model inputs aged zero seconds; winter/summer and pre/post shock grading. Champion winter failure. |
| energy_iv_marks | Range and version checks across three curves; four +8-point corrections. No option P&L attribution possible. |
| energy_position_snapshots, energy_limits | Opening snapshots plus corrected trade-time flows reconstruct intraday net exposure; Brent above available limit. Snapshots have 32/172/179 rows across 10/11/12 Nov. |
| energy_settlements | All 486 rows across nine curves profiled for price ranges; not used as intraday execution benchmarks. |
| energy_da_prices | 72 hourly rows and publication times inspected. 11 Nov peak GBP 233.90/MWh at 19:00 was published the prior day; delivery time is not quote time. |
| energy_lineage and remaining derived views | All 33 dependency records valid/active. Booking, model, strip and currency-factor definitions inspected; current-time convenience views avoided in fixed-date execution results. Not a full independent reconciliation of every derived view. |
